title: Webhook audit: ordering, idempotency, and DLQ strategy
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Background: Several internal postmortems and customer reports show gaps in our audit-webhook delivery guarantees: out-of-order events for a single customer/route, duplicate events ingested by SIEMs, and lack of clear dead-letter handling. These issues risk incorrect forensic trails and slow incident response for security teams that ingest Redwood audit streams into Splunk/Datadog/SIEMs.

Goal: Define and implement a delivery model for audit webhooks that provides per-customer ordering guarantees (monotonic order for events generated by a single tenancy), practical deduplication (idempotency at receivers), and a robust Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) + escalation path when third-party endpoints are unreachable or return permanent failures.

Constraints and non-goals: We cannot require partners to change their receivers; therefore server-side mechanisms should work with best-effort receiver behavior. Exactly-once semantics across arbitrary third-party receivers are out of scope; aim for at-least-once with strong dedupe controls and clear visibility. Must work with existing Dedicated and Private deployment modes.

Design proposal summary:
- Envelope: All audit events will include an immutable event_id (UUID v4), a monotonic sequence_number per-customer-route, timestamp, and HMAC signature (sha256) of the serialized payload using a rotating key.
- Ordering: Maintain per-customer-route ordering by attaching sequence_number; server will prefer in-order delivery but allow concurrent delivery for unrelated routes. If an out-of-order response is returned (e.g., receiver processed later sequence before earlier), downstream consumers can use sequence_number to reorder.
- Deduplication: Use idempotency window on Redwoods side: keep a bounded dedupe cache for event_id for 7 days (configurable). Receiver retries will be suppressed if event_id already acknowledged. Use a combination of LRU cache + persistent append-only index for high-volume customers. For small customers rely on in-memory dedupe with fallback to a bloom filter for memory efficiency.
- Retry policy: Exponential backoff with full-jitter, initial=1s, max_interval=15m, max_attempts=10. Respect receiver Retry-After and 429 semantics. For 4xx (400, 401, 403) treat as permanent depending on code: 401/403 => rotate keys/notify customer, 400/422 => inspect payload and surface to support.
- DLQ and Escalation: After max_attempts, move event to per-customer DLQ (S3 bucket in hosted, local file in Private) with metadata including last error, http status, and delivery logs. Trigger alert to on-call and create a ticket in support workflow for high-volume DLQ (>100 events/hr). Provide an operator UI in Console to requeue, inspect, or redact DLQ entries.
- Security: Webhooks must be delivered over TLS with cert pinning optional. HMAC-SHA256 signing with rotating keys exposed to customer via Console and Audit Logs. Rotate signing keys every 90 days by default with a grace period of 7 days.
- Observability: New metrics: deliver_attempts_total, deliver_success_total, deliver_failures_by_code, dlq_moves_total, dedupe_hits_total, average_delivery_latency_ms. Dashboards and alerting playbooks will be added: DLQ rate, retry storm detection, and per-customer failure heatmap.
- Failure modes & mitigation: Protect against hot-tenant storms by per-customer rate limits and circuit breaker on repeated 5xxs. Use backpressure to avoid OOM on servers: limit in-flight webhook batches per worker and persist overflow to durable queue (Kafka/SQS).

Trade-offs considered:
- Exactly-once vs at-least-once: Exactly-once requires receiver cooperation (ack tokens or transactional endpoints). We chose at-least-once + dedupe to remain compatible with customer endpoints.
- Statefulness: Per-customer ordering requires state (sequence tracking). We keep this state sharded and sharded sequence offsets persisted to the metadata store to survive restarts.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) API + Envelope: Add event_id, sequence_number, signature fields to audit payload. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4631)
2) Router + Queueing: Add per-customer routing key and bounded in-memory queue with overflow to durable queue. Implement circuit-breaker on 5xx. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1912)
3) Dedup + DLQ: LRU dedupe cache + S3 DLQ writer + requeue tool in Console. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/979)
4) Observability + Alerts: Grafana dashboards and pager playbook. (Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal/apps/dashboards/alerts-audit-delivery)

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for envelope signing/verification and sequence incrementing.
- Integration tests against a fake SIEM that returns configurable responses (200, 429, 500, 401) and asserts expected retries and DLQ behavior.
- Staging run with 5 production customers (opt-in) sending live audit traffic for 48 hours to validate dedupe and ordering.

Acceptance criteria:
- No customer sees >1% additional duplicate events vs baseline (measured by dedupe hits) during staging.
- DLQ entries are created and requeueable from Console.
- Metrics and alerts configured and tested in staging.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood-internal.com/audit-delivery/design-v2
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4631 (API), https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1912 (router), https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/979 (DLQ)
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal/apps/dashboards/alerts-audit-delivery
- Postmortem reference: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=80421

Open questions:
- Per-route strict ordering: do we require strict in-order delivery for all routes or offer it as opt-in for customers that need it? (proposal: opt-in with higher resource cost)
- Deduplication window size vs storage cost for high-throughput customers: propose 7 days default, can reduce for high-volume tenants.

2026-03-12 - Design decision: Opt-in strict ordering for customers that enable it in Console. Default is best-effort with sequence numbers for consumer-side reordering.
